Stated Claim / Post Context:
Dolly Parton’s niece named brand ambassador for her estate

Danielle Parton, the niece of Dolly Parton, has been named a brand ambassador following the death of her aunt, according to a video announcement released Wednesday.

Actual Article Body:
What This Story Is About

Catch Up

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Danielle Parton, the niece of Dolly Parton, has been named a brand ambassador following the death of her aunt, according to a video announcement released Wednesday.

In the video, Danielle Parton introduced herself and discussed her family background and career. “Hey y’all, I’m Danielle Parton. I grew up in East Tennessee in a family y’all have heard of,” she said. “We know hard work, faith, humor and big dreams are simply part of who we are.”

Danielle Parton said Dolly Parton was her aunt, though she referred to her as “Aunt Granny.” “She loved us deeply, believed in big dreams, and she always encouraged me to find my way in this world,” Danielle Parton said.

Danielle Parton is a commercial airline pilot and military veteran. She said her aunt’s encouragement led her toward a career in the sky. “For me, that path led to the sky. I became a pilot, I served my nation for 20 years in the National Guard, and I built a career in aviation that I’m incredibly proud of to this day,” she said.

Danielle Parton began her aviation career as a flight attendant with American Airlines and later Southwest Airlines before pursuing her goal of becoming a pilot. She joined the Air National Guard, serving with the 118th Wing in Nashville, the 123rd Airlift Wing in Louisville, Kentucky, and the 164th Airlift Wing in Memphis.

During her military career, she flew C-130 and C-5 aircraft around the world and in combat. She became an Aircraft Commander in 2012, deployed multiple times and logged thousands of hours in the cockpit. She was a Distinguished Graduate of C-5 Initial Qualification and received the Combat Action Medal, the Air Medal and the Commodore’s List of Flying Excellence during Undergraduate Pilot Training.

She served as Chief of Public Affairs for the 118th Wing and retired from the military in 2025 after 20 years of service.

In 2014, Danielle Parton joined one of the world’s largest commercial airlines. She continues to fly the Boeing 787. “I still fly commercially, something I love and intend to keep doing,” she said.

Danielle Parton is also the founder of Shine Girl, a moonshine distillery and retail hub in Pigeon Forge. “In addition to being a pilot, I’m also the creator of Shine Girl, my moonshine brand in East Tennessee, specifically in Pigeon Forge, exactly two doors now from Dollywood,” she said.

Both sides of Danielle Parton’s family, the Partons and Nolands, have deep roots in Sevier County, Tennessee, and generations of her family were connected to the making of moonshine. Her grandfather, Lee Parton, was known to make moonshine to help support his family, while her great-grandfather, Wiley Noland, made moonshine in a cabin on the family property. Wiley Noland’s brother, Sheriff Ray Noland, was known for shutting down illegal moonshine operations in the area.

After years of developing the concept, navigating a trademark battle, and purchasing a failed distillery, Danielle Parton launched Shine Girl in 2022. The brand includes recipes that incorporate ingredients such as honey, sugar and molasses alongside corn.

Danielle Parton said her aunt’s death has prompted her to reflect on her family’s legacy. “Like so many of you, losing her has changed something for me,” she said. “It made me think of the stories, values, and lessons that she left behind, and the responsibility that our family has to care for them.”

She said she does not intend to speak for Dolly Parton. “I would never try to speak for Dolly, and I’m not crazy enough to try to fill her shoes. God knows I couldn’t walk on them without killing myself,” she said. “What I can do is share the woman that I knew. I can tell some of the stories of her, the stories behind the global icon, and support the people carrying forward the work that she cared for and created to make sure what she built continues to bring people joy.”

Danielle Parton said she will continue her careers in aviation and as an entrepreneur alongside her new role. “I’m still a pilot, I’m still a girl boss, and I’m still Danielle,” she said. “But I’m also still a Parton, and I’m so grateful to help care for a legacy that means so much, not only to my family, but to all of you.”

Danielle Parton was born in East Tennessee and spent part of her early childhood in Washington State before returning home. She attended school in East Tennessee and graduated from Belmont University in Nashville in 1998 with a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration, becoming the first woman in the Parton family to earn a four-year college degree.
